maria-support: FYI AcmeHealth (enterprise) just escalated. Streaming responses from /v1/stream are getting truncated — final JSON is incomplete and "finish_reason" is absent. Customer says ~30% of sessions. Repro attached. Escalating to eng-runtime.

maria-support: Repro curl they used:
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-large","prompt":"summarize...","max_tokens":512}' \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream"
```

lucas-qa: I ran that against staging and saw the same pattern. Stream ends mid-object, last bytes are something like:
```
data: {"id":"r1","choices":[{"text":"...","index":0}],"finish_reason":
```
then connection closes. No trailing "}" or final event.

ashley-sre: Edge logs around the time show upstream socket closed right after final write from app: 
```
[2026-03-16T18:12:04Z] fastly POP iad: UPSTREAM_CONN_CLOSED status=200 upstream=10.2.8.14:443 bytes=1523 duration=412ms
```
Looks like the edge cut the connection before the last few bytes hit the client.

simon-eng: Two quick hypotheses: 1) runtime didn't flush the trailing newline/double-newline for SSE (SSE needs \n\n to terminate an event), so proxy buffered; 2) Fastly/edge idle or chunking behavior closed the socket before buffer drain. We should verify if server wrote final sentinel and invoked a flush.

lucas-qa: I captured a tcpdump between app and edge — the app's final write contains the JSON close, but it's missing the extra \n\n. tcpdump excerpt (hex->ascii):
```
data: {"id":"r1","choices":[{"text":"...","index":0}],"finish_reason":"stop"}\n
<FIN from fastly>
```
The FIN arrives immediately after a single \n, not the double newlines SSE expects, so some bytes might be dropped in transit.

ashley-sre: Practical mitigation for customer: ask them to retry with `curl -N --no-buffer` and ensure their client tolerates incomplete final events (e.g., attempt reconnect and fetch remainder with a resume token). Also request their Fastly POP (they provided `iad`) and exact timestamps — thanks. We'll also add guidance to recommend explicit sentinel event (server-side) as a short-term workaround: `event: stream_end\ndata: DONE\n\n`.

simon-eng: Agreed. Plan: add runtime change to always emit final sentinel event, ensure we flush (fsync-equivalent) on final SSE write, and add a metric `sse_final_flush_missed` so we can alert on regressions. I'll prepare a small hotfix branch.

devops-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-1423. Assigned to eng-runtime (simon-eng). Pager duty notified.

ashley-sre: For now, I'm telling the customer we'll prioritize a hotfix. Also asked them to share their tcpdump and any intermediary (Fastly) logs for 2026-03-16T18:12:03Z.

maria-support: Customer responded with POP = iad and timestamp 2026-03-16T18:12:03Z. They attached truncated stream and curl. Uploading to ticket.

simon-eng: I'll push a patched image that appends the explicit sentinel and forces a final flush. Requesting QA to validate with same POP and their curl. If QA green, we can roll to prod with a controlled rollout. Assigned to @simon-eng.

[thread status: assigned -> eng-runtime, customer notified of workaround, incident open]
